### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc845f936ca2f27d685a7069c7f731d25d155d1c` — the merge of head `7e516c3dcdf34536b4aa39aa1e25b3b1e604a06f` into base `42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc845f936ca2f27d685a7069c7f731d25d155d1c && git checkout cc845f936ca2f27d685a7069c7f731d25d155d1c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209 7e516c3dcdf34536b4aa39aa1e25b3b1e604a06f && git checkout -B drift-repro 42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209 && git merge --no-ff 7e516c3dcdf34536b4aa39aa1e25b3b1e604a06f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 42ff86f67723f5cd6b275bc4ddbb10f05e8c4209` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e516c3dcdf34536b4aa39aa1e25b3b1e604a06f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/by-id-write-unreadable-not-found.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx (prose face, the one added sentence), .changeset/write-refusal-read-door-parity.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts (`DelegatedAdminGate`, every arm), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`getCallerPreImage`, `absentUnderCallerRead`, `readUnlessRefused`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts (`addressedByIdWriteId`, `readRowById`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/record-row-write-probe.ts (`isRowWriteProbe`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts (`assertEngineOwnedWriteAllowed`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`declaredHttpStatus`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts (`assertVersionOf`, route (i), commit f95d0dbad5), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getData`, `updateData`, `deleteData`), docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md (D12 and its two amendments), docs/adr/0103-managedby-write-policy-and-engine-write-guard.md (D1, D2)

Inputs: the PR body, its five-file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge base `b3d1415055`, and the head's check-runs. Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions, not the dev's private report.

### ① Derived judgments

The change is one `try/catch` around the ADR-0090 D12 gate's `assert` in the engine authorization middleware, plus the helper `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal`. The helper is entered only from the catch. It hands back the gate's own refusal unchanged unless all of these hold: the refusal declares a 4xx (`declaredHttpStatus`), the operation is not a row-write probe, and `addressedByIdWriteId` names an id (a top-level by-id `update` or `delete`; a nested write, the referential clear, an insert and a predicate write name none). Then it asks `getCallerPreImage` for that id, which is the caller's own by-id read through the engine (`readRowById` → `ql.findOne` under the caller's context — the same read the HTTP by-id door `getData` issues, and the same read step 2.7 shares). A read that throws a declared 4xx becomes the answer; a read that answers (a row or `null`) leaves the gate's refusal as it was; anything else the read throws propagates.

What answers change, by caller class, for a by-id update or delete on a governed object:

- Reads and writes the object, no administration: the read answers, so the gate's own sentence stands. Unchanged.
- Reads only: the same. Unchanged.
- Writes without reading: the gate's sentence becomes the read door's refusal — the same `{status, code, message}` its by-id read gives for every id — for an existing row, an unknown id, and with or without a version token. With a token the OCC comparison (route (i), commit f95d0dbad5) already answered that read refusal for a mismatched token on an existing row and stands down for an unknown id, whose write now answers the same; the no-token write now matches too. This is the rule's class.
- Neither reads nor writes: as above.
- Create-only: an insert names no row and keeps the gate's sentence; its by-id update or delete takes the read refusal. Consistent with the rule.
- Tenant-level administrator: `isTenantLevelAdmin` returns before any refusal; the wrapper is never entered. Unchanged (an unknown id answers the door's `404`).
- Organization administrator: holds a read grant on the assignment objects, so the read answers and the gate's own sentence stands, for a row and for no row. Unchanged, as the brief's rule states.
- Delegate (`adminScope` holder): if the delegate reads the object, every gate answer is unchanged. If not, every refusal the gate gives it — including the scope arms, which word their refusals after the target row and the set it names — now becomes the read refusal. This class is covered by the rule and is an improvement; it is not pinned by a test (see ③).
- System context: bypassed before the gate; a flow-run or app-automation system identity is refused earlier by `assertFlowSystemIdentityWriteAllowed`, which is not wrapped and reads no row. Unchanged.
- Principal-less user context: the gate refuses, the read is refused on the same ground, so the read refusal answers; row-independent. Consistent.
- Another organization's caller: its read of the object decides — refused, the read refusal; answered, the gate's sentence. Consistent with the rule.
- Row-write probe (the record field-access `writable` verdict): excluded by `isRowWriteProbe`; the verdict is refused either way.

`Clause-②: no` is right. Every answer that changes was a refusal and stays one with the same status and code; what moves is the sentence (and the error's name on the delegate arm). Nothing refused is admitted and nothing admitted is refused: the wrapper sits on the catch path only, a read that answers restores the gate's refusal byte for byte, and `stampWriter` still runs only after `authorize` returns. No accept set narrows. Precedent #28615 (a refusal swapped for another refusal on an existing door) applies.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. No spec key, published schema, export or default changes; one package moves; the change is a sentence on a path that was already a refusal. The changeset carries both declaration lines; the PR body carries the same two.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The narrowed public wording ("cannot read the object", not "cannot see the row") is exactly what is enforced. The swap keys on `getCallerPreImage` throwing a declared 4xx — the caller's read of the object refused — and never on a `null` answer (a row absent from the caller's read). A caller who reads the object keeps the gate's own answer whatever the row. The changeset body ("whose read of the object is refused"), the docs sentence ("a caller refused reading the object … a caller who reads the assignment object gets the administration refusal's own sentence") and the code say the same thing. One incompleteness, not a contradiction: the gate governs three objects (`sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_member`) and the wrapper covers all three identically, while the changeset and the docs sentence name the two assignment objects only. The third object's gate refusal is row-independent before and after, so the prose claim is true of what it names; a follow-up may widen the sentence.
- The engine-owned write guard (ADR-0103 D2, `assertEngineOwnedWriteAllowed`) runs before the gate and is not wrapped. Its exclusion holds on a stronger ground than reachability: it judges the schema's `managedBy` bucket, the operation and the context, and reads no row, so its answer never varies by id. Whether or not the HTTP exposure answer keeps it unreached for a given object, it opens no existence boundary.
- Suites ran at the parent commit `04e42a7b06`: `git diff 04e42a7b06 7e516c3dcd` is one line, the changeset's title; no code, test or docs byte differs between the two, so the parent's runs describe this head. The head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts (below).
- Test evidence. Plugin, real engine over SQL with the real `SecurityPlugin`: per object × verb, a caller with no grant and a caller with write-without-read — the by-id read refused as the precondition, the row's write and an unknown id's write both `toEqual` that refusal in code, status, message and name, the row untouched; controls: a reader keeps the gate's sentence for a row and for no row, an administrator updates and gets `404` for no row, an insert keeps the gate's sentence. Showcase HTTP door: the stale-token families now compare status, code and sentence for every family, the assignment object included, for a row, for no row and without a token, across `If-Match` and `expectedVersion`; a new organization-administrator control pins the gate's sentence on `PATCH` for a row and for no row. Not pinned: a delegate who cannot read the object, and the third governed object. Both are covered by the same wrapper line, so the pins would guard against a future narrowing of the wrapper, not a gap in this head.
- Check-runs on `7e516c3dcd` at the time of this record: every completed run is `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, every scoped lint, Type Check source/consumer/debt-ledger, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 7/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links). Still running: Test Core shards 1–6 and 8, and Type Check · workspace. No run has failed.
- `reviewFace` on the file list decides no face (no published schema, no governed path, `Clause-②: no` with no arm); the tier is the one the ruling of record owes for the boundary, as the brief states.

### ④ Design judgment

- An ALLOW turned into a refusal: none. The wrapper is reachable only after the gate has thrown; the pass path is byte-identical. Non-governed objects and non-governed operations return from `assert` before `authorize` and never throw.
- A read fault turned into a different refusal: no. A read that throws with a declared status of 500 or more, or with no declared status at all, propagates as raised — an outage is neither an answer nor a refusal, the same discipline step 2.7 and `readUnlessRefused` follow. A gate throw with no declared status or with a 5xx status is handed back untouched. A declared 4xx from the read is, by construction, what the read door answers this caller for that id, so the parity holds for it too.
- A race between the gate and the caller read: none that changes an outcome. The gate's refusal on the rule's class is decided on the caller and the object; the extra read comes after it and, whichever way it answers, the result is a refusal and nothing is written. A row appearing or vanishing between the two reads cannot turn an object-level read refusal into an answer.
- Performance: one extra by-id read, on the refused path only, for by-id update and delete on three objects. The pre-image memo it leaves is on an operation context that is then discarded. Negligible, and the read is the same one the admitted path already pays at step 2.7.
- A path where the gate's answer still differs by row existence for a caller who cannot read the object: none found. Every arm of the gate — the anchor refusal, the principal-less refusal, the membership-object refusal, the organization-level arm, the delegate arms and the plain-grant refusal — throws a declared 4xx, and every one of them is wrapped; for a caller whose read is refused, every one becomes that read refusal, for any id. Callers who read the object are outside the rule by its own statement.
- Version tokens: the comparison answers before the engine is entered. For the rule's class a mismatched token on an existing row already answered the read refusal (route (i)); on an unknown id it stands down and the write now answers the same refusal; a matching token proceeds to the same write. The dogfood pin compares all three carriers for the whole body.

No must-fix. Two rule-level observations are recorded in ③ (the prose naming two of three governed objects; the two unpinned classes), neither of which changes what this head enforces.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-f`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
